title: Floating-Point Values and Decimal Precision
learningObjectives: Explain the central rules behind floating-point values and decimal precision in C.
Identify the relevant types, declarations, operators or library facilities.
Trace a worked example and explain its result.
Recognize common mistakes, portability concerns and unsafe assumptions.
Apply the concept in a small program and test normal and boundary cases.

understand.concept: C provides float, double and long double floating types. Many decimal fractions cannot be represented exactly in binary floating point, so calculations may contain rounding error. The precision and range of each type are implementation characteristics. Floating-point values should not generally be compared for exact equality after calculations.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding precision is important for measurements, scientific calculations and money-like values. A program must choose an appropriate representation and comparison strategy rather than assuming decimal fractions are exact.
understand.analogy: Think of a type as a contract that describes what kind of value an object can hold and which operations make sense for it.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only an introduction; C types also determine representation, conversions, alignment and constraints.

explain.narrative:
C provides float, double and long double floating types. Many decimal fractions cannot be represented exactly in binary floating point, so calculations may contain rounding error. The precision and range of each type are implementation characteristics. Floating-point values should not generally be compared for exact equality after calculations.

Understanding precision is important for measurements, scientific calculations and money-like values. A program must choose an appropriate representation and comparison strategy rather than assuming decimal fractions are exact.

When reviewing code, identify the declared types first, then trace conversions and the exact expression being evaluated. Compile with warnings enabled and test boundary values. Do not rely on assumptions about another compiler or machine.

practise.guidedTask: Calculate several decimal fractions and print them with different precisions. Compare the displayed values with the underlying approximation.
practise.independentTask: Implement a tolerance-based comparison for measured floating-point values. For financial totals, compare the trade-offs of integer minor units and decimal arithmetic requirements.
hints: Binary floating point cannot exactly represent every decimal fraction.
Display precision and stored precision are different.
Use tolerances appropriate to the scale of the problem.
Check for non-finite values when inputs may produce them.
Do not use binary floating point for exact monetary accounting without a deliberate representation strategy.
